articles.headline: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors
keyFacts: Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick criticized his bench players after they nearly squandered a 16-point lead late in a game against the Toronto Raptors.
Redick stated he had to send his starters back onto the court to secure the 131-125 victory.
Redick said he will not make the same mistake of clearing his bench early in future games.
body: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors originally appeared on The Sporting News .
Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The Los Angeles Lakers had one of their best performances of their 2026-27 season so far against the Toronto Raptors. They went up by as much as 26 points and led by 16 points in the final two minutes of the game. This prompted Lakers head coach JJ Redick to clear out his bench to see out the game.

Unfortunately, the bench unit did not live up to expectations, as they almost blew the lead. This led to Redick sending Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, and Matisse Thybulle back in to see out the game and get the 131-125 win.
JJ Redick admits he is disappointed by the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the game

It is normal for coaches to send in their bench players to see out a game, especially when they have a lead as big as 16 points. However, what the Lakers' bench players showed against the Raptors was a bad sign, which is why Redick is putting his foot down.

He does not like what happened in the game against the Raptors, especially since he wanted to rest his starters. Unfortunately for the Lakers, Redick had to send the starters back in because he wanted to secure the win rather than give up the massive lead in just a couple of minutes.
MORE: JJ Redick speaks on what it's like seeing Luka Doncic dominate up close

Thankfully for Redick and the Lakers, the starters were stable enough to get the result. It was a big win for the Lakers, but it does show some bad signs if the mediocre bench performances continue, which could have a long-term effect on the players and the coaching staff's approach to games.
"I won’t make that mistake again. I’ll leave the guys in. You got to play to the final buzzer," Redick said about sending his bench in after getting a 16-point lead .

It will be a big lesson for the Lakers moving forward, not only for Redick, but also for the players. When they are playing with a massive lead late into the game, the players must learn how to deal with the pressure and close out the win. It should never be stepping off the gas, they just need to balance their aggression with some semblance of control to get the win without any issue.

articles.headline: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh defends Justin Herbert amid league lead in interceptions
keyFacts: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw two interceptions in a loss to the Rams, bringing his league-leading total to 10 picks this season.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh stated he has not considered benching Herbert and described the team's struggles as a collective issue.
Herbert acknowledged his poor decisions and turnovers, stating he must work to improve his performance moving forward.
body: The Chargers dropped to 0-7 with a 24-9 home loss to the Rams on Sunday, and the conversation around quarterback Justin Herbert's ball security reached a new level.

Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards but threw two interceptions and now leads the NFL with 10 picks through seven games. He has thrown one in every contest this season, while posting just five touchdowns.

Afterward, head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked whether he had considered benching Herbert. His answer was direct: "No." Instead, he framed the issues as a collective problem rather than an individual one.

"First of all, it's a team effort. We're gonna look at the film. We're gonna address our issues where we can get better, and that's just keep working. That's highly motivated and dedicated to getting this right," Harbaugh said. "We're the only ones that have had the opportunity to change it, to fix it, and that's what we're gonna do."

Herbert himself was straightforward about the numbers. "That's part of the game, and it's the unfortunate part of where we're at. And I'd love to have played better and made better decisions, but, you know, I haven't, and that's something I have to work on and continue to get better at," he told reporters after the game.

Herbert's two interceptions led directly to 10 points for the Rams. The second pick was a low point, as he completely missed underneath defender Trent McDuffie and threw the ball directly into coverage on a pass he intended for tight end Charlie Kolar.

Herbert entered 2026 with some of the lowest turnover rates of his career. From 2020 through 2025, he turned the ball over on just 1.7% of offensive plays. That rate has climbed significantly this year.
The Chargers' offense has failed to score a touchdown for two consecutive weeks. Until Herbert cleans up the giveaways, the team's search for its first victory will remain difficult to obtain.

articles.headline: Haskell backs Borthwick, Pollock as England prepare for Nations Championship
keyFacts: Former England international James Haskell stated that Steve Borthwick is the right head coach to lead England through the 2027 Rugby World Cup.
England is preparing to play matches against Australia, Japan, and New Zealand in November ahead of the Nations Championship finals weekend.
Haskell expressed excitement about rising star Henry Pollock and hopes the back-row player receives more opportunities to play for England.
body: England Rugby: Steve Borthwick and Henry Pollock backed by James Haskell ahead of Nations Championship fixtures

James Haskell believes Steve Borthwick is the right man to lead England at the 2027 Rugby World Cup and shares his excitement over rising star Henry Pollock ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures against Australia, Japan and New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham
Monday 2 November 2026 06:01, UK
James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November.

Borthwick oversaw England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign earlier this year, with four losses from their five matches, but despite growing pressure the RFU have publicly expressed their support for Borthwick through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.
This month, England will face Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of Finals Weekend, which takes place November 27-28 at Twickenham.
Former England international Haskell, who earned 77 Test caps between 2007 and 2019, insists it is not the time to change the head coach.
"The RFU have got behind Steve Borthwick, and rightly so," Haskell told Sky Sports.
"I think he's the right man for the job."
Borthwick oversaw a 12-game unbeaten streak ahead of the 2026 Six Nations, and Haskell insists the change in performance is not as stark as the critics might suggest.
"It's never as bad as you think it is and it's never as good as you think it is," he said.
"I think there's a lot of talent, and without being a super nerd - which rugby pundits often can be - if you look at the stats, we create lots of opportunities.
"When we were on our unbeaten run of 12 games, 83 per cent of the time we got into the 22-metre line, we took away points.
"When we were losing games, we were making the same opportunities but coming away with points less than 33 per cent of the time.
"And that's the fine margins."
Pollock has that 'X-factor'
Haskell also praised the ego and style of rising star Henry Pollock.

The Northampton Saints back-row who made headlines by becoming the first rugby union player to sign for Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency back in March, could be given more international chances in the coming weeks.
"He's definitely got that X-factor, in terms of the way he plays," said Haskell.
"He's probably the most talked about rugby player at the moment. He creates opinion and challenges opinion - and that's what makes the world go round now.
"But when he gets opportunities on the field, he delivers… I'm very excited that he will hopefully get more of a chance to play for England.
"It will challenge some of the stuffier, more stoic sides of the upper echelons, and of the fanbase, who like their sports stars manageable and with a bit of ego, but not too much.
"If someone could bring that cohesion together, keep raising awareness and building superstars like Henry Pollock, you're going to be in a great place."
